newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus police disperse crowds at checkpoint.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus police disperse crowds at checkpoint.

text.p: Police said they used teargas on Sunday to disperse Greek Cypriots trying to prevent diplomats from crossing into the Turkish-held area of the divided island through a United Nations checkpoint in the capital.
U.N. spokesman Waldemar Rokosewski said two members of the peacekeeping force also were assaulted by demonstrators who sprayed a caustic substance in their faces.
"They have been medically examined and they are O.K.," he said. "This incident shall be protested at a political and a police level." Demonstrators denied attacking any U.N. personnel.

Five people were taken to hospital with breathing problems after the police used teargas to disperse the up to 50 people who gathered at the U.N.-controlled Ledra Palace checkpoint in central Nicosia. They were later discharged.

Demonstrators wanted to block the checkpoint to protest what they said was the refusal of the Turkish Cypriot administration in the north of the island to allow two Maronite Christians into the southern government-controlled areas for medical treatment.
Some thumped on the bonnets of two cars belonging to diplomats of the British High Commission and the U.S. embassy when they appeared at the checkpoint to cross over, police said.
"They blocked off the road and some lay in the street to prevent the diplomatic cars from crossing into the occupied areas," police spokesman Glafcos Xenos told Reuters.
"We used the appropriate force to remove them and restore order," he added.
Greek Cypriots have been staging weekend demonstrations at the checkpoint for the past three months to discourage foreigners from visiting the north.
"This is totally without grounds," said Marios Matsakis, an MP for the centre-right Diko party. Matsakis is actively involved in the protests. "We never saw any UN personnel injured.
Matsakis accused police of "acting unreasonably." Demonstrators will block access again next week, he said.
"Unless the Turks allow these two people over we will not just protest, we will demand that human rights are respected," he said.
Police have instructions to keep the access point open.

The island has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in the wake of a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece. Turkish Cypriots declared a breakaway state in the north in 1983, which is recognised only by Ankara.
